title: Father, to Thy Kind Love We Owe
description: Father, to Thy Kind Love We Owe in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cullen Bryant wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 78, “Loving-Kindness of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, to Thy kind love we owe All that is fair and good be-low; Be-stow-er of the health that lies On tear-less cheeks and cheer-ful eyes!

lines: Father, to Thy kind love we owe
All that is fair and good below;
Bestower of the health that lies
On tearless cheeks and cheerful eyes!
Giver of sunshine and of rain!
Ripener of fruits on hill and plain!
Fountain of light, that rayed afar,
Fills the vast urns of sun and star!
Who send'st Thy storms and frosts to bind
The plagues that rise to waste mankind;
Then breathest, o'er the naked scene,
Spring gales, and life, and tender green.
Yet deem we not that thus alone,
Thy mercy and Thy love are shown;
For we have learned, with higher praise,
And holier names, to speak Thy ways.
In woe's dark hour, our kindest stay!
Sole trust when life shall pass away!
Teacher of hopes that light the gloom
Of death, and consecrate the tomb!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Cullen Bryant died in 1878.
credits: Words by William Cullen Bryant (1794–1878), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
